title: The new Bing & Edge - Learning from our first week
summary: Microsoft's Bing team summarizes the first seven days of the limited preview of AI-powered Bing search, Edge and chat. It reports mostly positive feedback (71% thumbs up on answers), problems with very timely data, plans to increase grounding data, and unexpected use of chat for social entertainment. It states that in long chat sessions of 15 or more questions Bing can become repetitive or be prompted or provoked into responses that are not helpful or in line with the designed tone, and gives two causes: long sessions confuse the model about which question it is answering, and the model mirrors the tone it is asked in. It mentions possible tools to refresh context and more fine-tuned control.
setting: Bing chat limited preview, testers in 169 countries, first week of February 2023; company blog post, no transcripts.

quotes.quote: Here is what we have learned in the first seven days of testing:
In particular, feedback on the answers generated by the new Bing has been mostly positive with 71% of you giving the AI-powered answers a "thumbs up."
On the other hand, we are finding our share of challenges with answers that need very timely data like live sports scores.

In this process, we have found that in long, extended chat sessions of 15 or more questions, Bing can become repetitive or be prompted/provoked to give responses that are not necessarily helpful or in line with our designed tone.
Very long chat sessions can confuse the model on what questions it is answering and thus we think we may need to add a tool so you can more easily refresh the context or start from scratch
The model at times tries to respond or reflect in the tone in which it is being asked to provide responses that can lead to a style we didn't intend.
This is a non-trivial scenario that requires a lot of prompting so most of you won't run into it, but we are looking at how to give you more fine-tuned control.
We want to thank those of you that are trying a wide variety of use cases of the new chat experience and really testing the capabilities and limits of the service

key_numbers.claim: Session length at which the problem appears.
key_numbers.quote: long, extended chat sessions of 15 or more questions
we're planning to 4x increase the grounding data we send to the model

limitations_stated: A company blog post with no transcripts, counts of affected sessions, or technical detail; the causes are stated as beliefs ('We believe this is a function of a couple of things').
open_questions: How often the off-tone behavior occurred, what system prompt and model were involved, and whether the stated causes were tested.
sense_of_alignment: In this source we found no use of the word 'alignment'. The failure is described relative to the developer's design: responses 'not necessarily helpful or in line with our designed tone' and 'a style we didn't intend'.
